schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT S.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM SALES S LEFT JOIN PRODUCT P ON S.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID WHERE S.SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' AND S.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES WHERE SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31') ORDER BY S.PRODUCT_ID

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT S.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM SALES S LEFT JOIN PRODUCT P ON S.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID WHERE S.SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' AND S.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES WHERE SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31') ORDER BY S.PRODUCT_ID
explanation: Q1 ensures all sales of a product are within the date range using MIN and MAX. Q2 ensures at least one sale in the range and no sales outside. A product with sales only in the range and another with sales in and out will show differences in edge cases.
counterexample_dsp: Product A has sales only in the range. Product B has sales in and out. Q1 excludes B, Q2 excludes B. However, if a product has sales in the range and no sales outside, both include it. If a product has no sales at all, both exclude it. But if a product has sales only in the range and another has sales in and out, they are both excluded.
